source_text: Εἶτα λέγει ὁ παρ᾿ αὐτῷ Ἰουδαῖος πρὸς τοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ λαοῦ πιστεύσαντας ὅτι χθὲς καὶ πρώην καὶ ὁπηνίκα τοῦτον ἐκολάζομεν βουκολοῦντα ὑμᾶς, ἀπέστητε τοῦ πατρίου νόμου, οὐδὲν ἀκριβὲς εἰδὼς ἐν οἷς ἔλεγεν, ὡς ἐδείξαμεν. μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα δοκεῖ μοι δεινότητος ἔχεσθαι τὸ ἢ πῶς ἄρχεσθε μὲν ἀπὸ τῶν ἡμετέρων ἱερῶν, προϊόντες δὲ αὐτὰ ἀτιμάζετε, οὐκ ἔχοντες ἄλλην ἀρχὴν εἰπεῖν τοῦ δόγματος ἢ τὸν ἡμέτερον νόμον; ἀληθῶς μὲν γὰρ Χριστιανοῖς ἡ εἰσαγωγή ἐστιν ἀπὸ τῶν ἱερῶν Μω(??)σέως καὶ τῶν προφητικῶν γραμμάτων· καὶ μετὰ τὴν εἰσαγωγὴν ἐν τῇ διηγήσει καὶ σαφηνείᾳ αὐτῶν ἐστι τοῖς εἰσαγομένοις ἡ προκοπὴ, ζητουσι τὸ „κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν“ μυστήριον, „χρόνοις αἰω νί οις“ σεσιγημένον (φανερωθὲν „δὲ νῦν“) ἐν ταῖς προφητικαῖς φωναῖς καὶ τῇ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐπιφανείᾳ. οὐχ, ὡς λέγετε δὲ, οἱ προϊόντες ἀτιμάζουσι τὰ ἐν νόμῳ γεγραμμένα ἀλλὰ πλείονα τιμὴν αὐτοῖς περιτιθέασιν ἀποδεικνύντες, ὅσον ἔχει βάθος σοφῶν καὶ ἀποῤῥήτων λόγων ἐκεῖνα τὰ γράμματα τὰ ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων οὐ τεθεωρημένα. τῶν ἐπιπολαιότερον καὶ μυθικώτερον αὐτοῖς ἐντυγχανόντων τί δὲ ἄτοπον τὸ ἀρχὴν τοῦ ἡμετέρου δόγματος, τουτέστι τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, εἶναι τὸν νόμον; ἅτε καὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν λέγοντος πρὸς τοὺς μὴ πιστεύοντας αὐτῷ· „εἰ ἐπιστεύετε Μωϋσεῖ, ἐπιστεύετε ἂν ἐμοί· περὶ γὰρ ἐμοῦ ἐκεῖνος ἔγραψεν. εἰ δὲ τοῖς ἐκείνου γράμμασιν οὐ πιστεύετε, πῶς τοῖς ἐμοῖς ῥήμασι πιστεύσετε;“ ἀλλὰ καὶ εἷς τῶν εὐαγγελιστῶν, ὁ Μάρκος, φησίν· „ἀρχὴ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς γέγραπται ἐν Ἡσαΐᾳ τῷ προφήτῃ· ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου“, δεικνὺς ὅτι ἡ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἀρχὴ τῶν Ἰουδαϊκῶν γραμμάτων ἤρτηται. τί οὖν καθ᾿ ἡμῶν λέγεται ὑπὸ τοῦ παρὰ τῷ Κέλσῳ Ἰουδαίου ἐν τῷ· εἴτε γὰρ προηγόρευσέ τις ὑμῖν ὅτι ἄρα ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ παῖς εἰς ἀνθρώπους ἀφίξεται, οὗτος ἡμέτερος ἦν ὁ προφήτης καὶ τοῦ ἡμετέρου θεοῦ· ποῖον δὲ ἔγκλημα χριστιανισμῷ ἐστιν, εἰ ὁ βαπτίσας τὸν Ἰησοῦν Ἰωάννης Ἰουδαῖος ἦν; οὐ γὰρ, ἐπεὶ Ἰουδαῖος ἦν, συνάγεται ὅτι δεῖ πάντα τὸν πιστεύοντα, εἴτ᾿ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν προσέρχεται τῷ λόγῳ εἴτε ἀπὸ Ἰουδαίων, [δεῖν] κατὰ τὸ γράμμα τὸν Μω(??)σέως τηρεῖν νόμον.
pass_a_gloss: Then the Jew in him says to those from the people who believed: yesterday and the day before (χθὲς καὶ πρώην), and when we were punishing (κολάζω) this man beguiling you (βουκολέω, lit. tending as cattle, metaph. cheat), you stood away (ἀφίστημι) from the ancestral law, knowing nothing accurate (ἀκριβής) in what he said, as we showed. After this, it seems to me to hold cleverness (δεινότης): or how do you begin from our sacred things (ἱερά), but advancing (προΐημι/πρόειμι) dishonour (ἀτιμάζω) them, not having another beginning (ἀρχή) of the doctrine (δόγμα) to name than our law? For truly for Christians the introduction (εἰσαγωγή) is from the sacred [writings] of Moses and the prophetic writings (γράμματα); and after the introduction, in their exposition (διήγησις) and clarification (σαφήνεια) is the progress (προκοπή) for those introduced, seeking the mystery (μυστήριον) according to revelation (ἀποκάλυψις), kept silent (σιγάω) in eternal times, (but now made manifest, φανερόω) in the prophetic utterances and the appearing (ἐπιφάνεια) of our Lord Jesus Christ. Not, as you say, do those advancing dishonour the things written in the law but put more honour (τιμή) around them, showing how much depth (βάθος) of wise and secret (ἀπόρρητος) words (λόγοι) those writings have, not contemplated (θεωρέω) by Jews, who read (ἐντυγχάνω) them rather superficially (ἐπιπολαιότερον) and mythically (μυθικώτερον). What is out of place that the law be the beginning of our doctrine, that is of the gospel (εὐαγγέλιον)? Since our Lord himself says to those not believing him: [John 5:46–47] if you believed Moses you would believe me; for about me that one wrote; if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words (ῥήματα)? One of the evangelists, Mark, says: [Mark 1:1–2] beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, as written in Isaiah the prophet: behold I send my messenger (ἄγγελος) before your face, who will prepare (κατασκευάζω) your way before you; showing that the beginning of the gospel hangs on (ἀρτάομαι) the Jewish writings. What then is said against us by the Jew in Celsus in: for if someone foretold (προαγορεύω) to you that the child of God (ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ παῖς) will arrive (ἀφικνέομαι) among men, this one was our prophet and our God’s? What charge (ἔγκλημα) is it to Christianity if John who baptized (βαπτίζω) Jesus was a Jew? For it is not concluded (συνάγεται), since he was a Jew, that every believer, whether from the nations he comes to (προσέρχομαι) the word (λόγος) or from Jews, must keep according to the letter the law of Moses.

lemmas.note: lit. tending as cattle, metaph. cheat

pass_b_english: Next, the Jew in his book says to those from the people who have believed: “Only yesterday or the day before, when we were punishing this man who was duping you, you turned away from the law of your fathers.” He said this without any accurate knowledge of what he was talking about, as we have shown.

After this, the following seems to me to show some cleverness: “Or how is it that you begin from our sacred writings, yet as you go on you dishonour them, though you can name no other starting point for your doctrine than our law?”

For it is true that for Christians the introduction comes from the sacred writings of Moses and the writings of the prophets; and after the introduction, the progress of those being introduced lies in the interpretation and clarification of these writings, as they seek the mystery “according to revelation,” “kept in silence through eternal ages,” but “now made manifest” in the words of the prophets and in the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 16:25–26). But those who advance do not, as you claim, dishonour what is written in the law. Rather they bestow greater honour on it, showing how great a depth of wise and secret sayings is held by those writings, which the Jews have not contemplated, since they read them rather superficially and as if they were myths.

And what is out of place in the law being the beginning of our doctrine, that is, of the gospel? For our Lord himself says to those who did not believe in him: “If you believed Moses, you would believe me; for he wrote about me. But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words?” (John 5:46–47). Moreover, one of the evangelists, Mark, says: “The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, as it is written in Isaiah the prophet: ‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you’ ” (Mark 1:1–2; Malachi 3:1; Exodus 23:20), showing that the beginning of the gospel depends on the Jewish writings.

What, then, is said against us by Celsus’s Jew in the words: “For if anyone foretold to you that the Son of God would come to men, that prophet was ours, and our God’s”? And what charge against Christianity is it if John, who baptized Jesus, was a Jew (Matthew 3:13–17)? For it does not follow, because he was a Jew, that every believer, whether he comes to the word from the Gentiles or from the Jews, must keep the law of Moses according to the letter.

added missing ‘For’ (γάρ) twice: ‘For it is true…’, ‘For it does not follow…’

choices.why: ‘οὐχ, ὡς λέγετε δέ, οἱ προϊόντες ἀτιμάζουσι’ now ‘those who advance do not, as you claim, dishonour’ (old wording could read as ‘as you say, it is not true’)
‘τὰ ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων οὐ τεθεωρημένα’ referred back to the writings (was moved onto ‘depth’); ‘μυθικώτερον’ now ‘as if they were myths’
Mark 1:2 inner quotation marked; Exodus 23:20 added beside Malachi 3:1 (LXX wording ‘before your face’); bible_refs and note updated

2.4: Origen's 'what charge is it if John, who baptized Jesus, was a Jew?' answers a point from Celsus that the Greek here does not quote. The English stays as Origen frames it, with no invented Celsus quotation

translator_notes: Copy-text: staged source_2.json section 4 (Koetschau 2.4); row complete. ‘Μω(??)σέως’ appears twice in the staged text with an unreadable character; read as Μωϋσέως (Moses), which the context requires. ‘αἰω νί οις’ is a line-break split of αἰωνίοις. The staged punctuation puts a full stop before ‘τῶν ἐπιπολαιότερον καὶ μυθικώτερον αὐτοῖς ἐντυγχανόντων’; this genitive phrase belongs with ‘ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων’ (the Jews, who read them superficially) and is translated so; the next sentence begins at ‘τί δὲ ἄτοπον’. ‘[δεῖν]’ is bracketed in the staged text as a doubled ‘must’ after ‘δεῖ’; translated once. ‘καὶ ὁπηνίκα’ in Celsus’s sentence is rendered ‘when’ (the καί joins the time phrases). ‘βουκολοῦντα’: lit. ‘herding like cattle’, used for ‘beguiling, cheating’; rendered ‘duping’. ‘ἱερῶν’ in Celsus’s words rendered ‘sacred writings’ because Origen’s reply takes it as ‘the sacred writings of Moses’; the bare sense is ‘sacred things’. ‘ὡς λέγετε’ is second person plural: Origen turns to address the Jew and those who share his view. ‘ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ παῖς’ (child or servant of God) rendered ‘the Son of God’ in the Jew’s words; the Jew uses παῖς, not υἱός. ‘εἴτε γάρ’ has no second εἴτε; taken as ‘for if’. ‘ἀποῤῥήτων λόγων’ rendered ‘secret sayings’. Romans 16:25–26 is quoted in fragments; ‘the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ’ may also echo 2 Timothy 1:10 (‘now made manifest through the appearing of our Saviour Christ Jesus’), possible only. Mark 1:2 attributes to Isaiah a text that is Malachi 3:1 (Septuagint numbering and English numbering agree here); Malachi 3:1 is cited beside the quotation. Matthew 3:13–17 is cited for the baptism of Jesus by John, a narrative reference rather than a quotation. ‘τῷ λόγῳ’ (comes to the word) is taken as the Christian message; a reference to the divine Word is possible, so it is left lower-case. Review: Mark 1:2’s wording ‘before your face’ (πρὸ προσώπου σου) matches Exodus 23:20 LXX verbatim, alongside Malachi 3:1; both cited inline.
